title: Research: two-source toggle DUO for the five-source connector — 72 queries at 74 adds (no new kappa)
head: 892b28a3358b16c9083036f71e1ef505ccf5d20a
body:
## Result (scoped finite; no new kappa)

One new complete call type added to the frozen universal-connector alphabet of `research/universal-connector-boundary` (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943, Ross Richardson):

    DUO_{j,k}: z += B_j x_j + B_k x_k     (j != k; one dispatch, sources read-only)

The only changed premise is that package's "no combined queries" rule, and the call is charged in full (two coefficient/source traversals, one target update cycle, one dispatch/entry-exit frame/head return). Everything else is unchanged: complete calls, arbitrary dirty rows, restoration of `z` and all scratch, paired `A_i` readouts, generic admissible operators.

**Exact finite result.** In the extended alphabet the five-source universal source word has unique Pareto profile (k calls, W toggle-adds) = **(10, 12)**, versus (12, 12) in the frozen singleton alphabet. For the frozen all-31-row batch this is **72 root queries at 74 toggle-adds instead of 74 at 74**: the support bound 72, unattainable in the singleton alphabet, is attained exactly here. In the price model `c_B = o + p`, `c_DUO = o + 2p`, `c_A = o + p` the completed batch costs `72o + 74p` against the frozen `74o + 74p` — strictly better for every `o > 0`, with total adds unchanged (the saving is exactly two per-call overheads `o`).

Lower bounds are complete for the domain, not heuristic: `k >= 10` because a complete census of all 7,888,725 nine-point sets of F2^5 finds **zero** difference covers (`C(s,2) >= 31` forces `s >= 9`, `k >= s`), and `W >= 12` by touch parity (`W` even, `W >= 10`; `W = 10` leaves only the all-unit `k = 10` words — the frozen 945 pairings, reproduced here with maximum coverage 31 of 32 — or `k <= 9` words that need the nonexistent `s <= 9` covers). The witness `steps 1,2,8,18,12,16,1,2,4,2`, prefixes `0,1,3,11,25,21,5,4,6,2,0` attains (10, 12), so it is Pareto-optimal. Tiny falsifying instance first: n=3 profile (5, 6) against (6, 6); n=4 side row (6, 8) against (8, 8).

## Task card

Selector nonce `bf263697e6c72cee43b6ded62be24c62`, track `recursive-interfaces`, card `connector-alphabet-change` (scope key `ff4f5113ed2256ab19ed`), **scope refined**: the card asked for "one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample" without naming the operation; the operation is fixed to the two-source combined toggle and the domains to n=3 (falsification first) then n=5 (the frozen priced instance). Full card: [notes/agent-18-duo-toggle-task-card.md](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/HEAD/notes/agent-18-duo-toggle-task-card.md). Base commit `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; head `892b28a3358b16c9083036f71e1ef505ccf5d20a`. Claim thread: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1403.

## Evidence and reproduction

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/duo-toggle-connector --check-only
# PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/duo-toggle-connector
# PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/duo-toggle-connector outcome=completed
```

Coverage: deterministic regeneration of `CERTIFICATE.json` (counts, histograms, sorted-record SHA256, witness words, the full 72-call batch word, pricing records); code-disjoint independent checks — brute-force `s = 9` scan of 7,888,725 sets expecting 0 full covers, the n=3 frontier by a second enumeration, the frozen 945-pairing control by restricted-growth words (histogram matches `research/universal-connector-boundary` exactly); symbolic replay of the emitted batch word; 12 dense dirty replays at L = 1, 2, 3 with seeded random noncommuting matrices and arbitrary dirty connector/output rows (forward and reverse order), checking restoration and all 31 output rows; 4 mutation controls (deleted call, shrunk DUO, misplaced readout, tampered record) all detected. Python 3.12/3.13, standard library only.

`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` on this Windows machine: 18/20 pass; the 5-then-1 errors are pre-existing and outside this diff — the fixture byte-compare breaks on `core.autocrlf=true` (fixture stores CRLF, git object LF) and `test_dependency_plan_and_runtime_failure` hits `os.killpg`, which does not exist on Windows. With `core.autocrlf` neutralized only the `killpg` test still fails.

## Limitations and obligations not checked

No physical supplier instance of this connector interface exists (the predecessor's own limitation, unchanged here); no compiler/tape integration, frames, owner admission, precision or outer analytic obligations; no proof assistant; no weighted global optimum beyond this price model. Words with `k >= 11` are outside the census and cannot beat already Pareto-minimal (10, 12). The 99,200-cover histogram (`(10,12)`: 8,500, `(10,14)`: 47,600, `(10,16)`: 26,600, `(10,18)`: 3,700) is `generate.py`'s claim with a recorded hash; the headline witness and both lower bounds are independently re-checked. The saving is exactly two per-call overheads: with zero per-call overhead the extension gains nothing.

## Overlap (refreshed at submission, 2026-10-14T02:19Z)

Complete pagination over 773 open PRs and 199 discussions. No PR or claim duplicates the read-only weight-2 combined toggle; later neighbors explicitly scope away from it: the atomic triple-sum connector (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1504, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1518), the second-dirty-root construction (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1412), and the S3 vector transport (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1467). Distinct from the mutable-source shear mechanism (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1340, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1370, discussion 1352), which needs temporarily writable source rows, and from the same-alphabet extension https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185 (`f(6) = 16`). No matches is not proof of novelty.
